data.why: The repo's own data/ and models/ folders only contain .gitkeep placeholders (no bundled LAS files or pretrained model), so a synthetic LAS2.0 file was written with realistic GR/RT/RHOB/NPHI/CALI curves, a clean hydrocarbon pay sand, a wet sand, a null/missing-data interval, and a caliper washout outlier for the app's upload widget.

goals: Upload a LAS well log and view standardized curve tracks (GR, resistivity, density-neutron) over a chosen depth window
Compute porosity (density, neutron, blended) and shale volume (VSH) using a selected GR model, and Archie water saturation
Run K-Means clustering on selected log curves to find facies-like groups and visualize them on the tracks
Cross-plot any two curves (e.g., RHOB vs NPHI) colored by a third variable such as GR or cluster label
Apply VSH/porosity/SW cutoffs to auto-pick net reservoir and net pay zones, get a zone summary and plain-English interpretation
Export interpreted results as CSV (petrophysics, zone summary, interval NTG/pay) and as a LAS file with added curves and flags

review.summary: The tree covers what PetroLog is for: from LAS upload through porosity/VSH/Archie SW, clustering and crossplots to cutoff-based net pay picking and exports. Its labels and phases are sound, every screen I sampled backs its node, and the second agent replayed all 11 tasks and 5 features. The only gaps are small: there is no ingest feature, f5 is somewhat oversized, and exports are placed inconsistently, so it can be filed as is.
